intent: Initial balanced geometry with 5 medium-sized sensors spread evenly across the front, moderate wheel track and radius, and compact body for stability and control. Expect integrator to tune a controller that completes the track with moderate speed and low line loss.
rationale: Starting from scratch with no prior data, I propose a balanced geometry with 5 sensors spread evenly across the front to cover the tape line well, using the medium sensor size (0.012 m) for a good balance of resolution and coverage. The wheel track is set moderately wide (0.14 m) for stability, with a medium wheel radius (0.035 m) to balance speed and torque. The body is compact but wide enough (0.12 m width, 0.18 m length) to provide stability without risking early off-track failure. Mass is set at 0.8 kg to keep inertia manageable. The intent is to provide a stable, well-sensed platform that the integrator can tune a controller on effectively. I expect this geometry to allow the integrator to develop a controller that completes the track with moderate speed and low line loss. Hypotheses include that 5 sensors with medium size will provide sufficient line detection and that the chosen wheel track and radius balance speed and control. I request measurements of completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, and completion_time to evaluate performance and line tracking quality.
